traveler: Emilia Massacesi (Emilia Portman / Em Port / Emi Massa)
title: The Record With No First Page: a Licenciada in Choreographic Composition, and a Second Name on the Pole
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: West of the City, Before Any Record

stops.name: Zona oeste, Buenos Aires Province, the tutu and the Shakira costume
stops.date_confidence: undated childhood memory, given in her own words in the NewsDigitales/Living interview; no town, no year. The pin sits on Morón, a conventional reference point for 'the west,' not an attested location; she names only the province.
stops.campa: She tells her own origin two ways in the same breath. First, a tutu in an older cousin's costume box, in a family where nobody danced; she will not give it back. Then, unprompted, the other memory: a childhood birthday, the neighborhood custom of arriving in costume, and she comes as Shakira, dancing wild and untrained, no lessons in Arabic dance, nothing borrowed. She grew up in the west of Buenos Aires Province, in schools that taught several forms in rotation, the custom then, she says, of another era: clásico español first, American tap alongside it, then a change of school and jazz. She does not name the town. No other source does either.
stops.quote: Creo que a través de un tutú... y era distinto a la danza del tutú, y era completamente otra cosa.
sources: NewsDigitales/Living interview transcript (~75 min), host Marisol, 2026
suggested_refs: The unnamed western Buenos Aires Province locality of her childhood

segments.name: A Record With No First Page

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the record that begins in the middle
stops.date_confidence: revised from an earlier pass, which read 2019 as the earliest attested year; independent alternativateatral production fichas now confirm dance credits in 2015, and her own interview supplies a training range of 2012-2018. No source anywhere, including this pass, carries a birth date or birthplace.
stops.campa: Every institutional account of her still begins in the middle. Her university's graduate profile gives a degree and a working biography and no birth date, no birthplace, no year of entry to the university itself, and no other reachable source supplies any of them either. What an earlier pass through this record got wrong was the floor under that gap: production fichas independently confirm her dancing in university company works as early as 2015, and her own interview account dates a broader formation, 2012 to 2018, in schools and companies before the university ever appears on paper. The birth date remains unrecorded. The dancing does not, and it starts earlier than this file once knew.

stops.name: Martín Rodríguez 444, the licenciatura
stops.date_confidence: placed at the earliest attested year of her working life; the degree itself carries no year on the graduate roll
stops.campa: The Universidad Nacional de las Artes grants her the Licenciatura en Composición Coreográfica, mención Danza. Its Departamento de Artes del Movimiento keeps a graduate roll, and the roll prints her name, her degree and her working biography with no year attached to any of it: not entry, not completion. She is a licenciada of a school whose published record does not say when she was in it. Where the school itself stands is not in doubt. It is at Martín Rodríguez 444, a few blocks off the Riachuelo in La Boca.
stops.quote: Creadora, bailarina, directora escénica y docente. Licenciada en Composición Coreográfica mención Danza.
stops.quote_source: UNA Departamento de Artes del Movimiento, graduate profile (author-supplied bio line), fetched 2026-08-16
sources: UNA Artes del Movimiento graduate profile, movimiento.una.edu.ar/graduadxs/massacesi-emilia_26

stops.name: Martín Rodríguez 444, two teachers named
stops.date_confidence: formation range 2012-2018 given in her own words in the interview; no year is attached to either teacher individually
stops.campa: Asked which teachers she still carries, she does not reach for a dean first. Gerardo Litvak, her composition teacher, for a severity that questions without cruelty: he detects everything, nothing gets past him, and he holds a steadiness inside a subjective art. Natalia Mucio, for technique, for a totality of commitment bordering on excessive, contagious anyway, without bias toward who gets to dance or what body does it. Neither claim carries a year. What she does date herself is the whole arc of formation, roughly 2012 to 2018, four programme tracks, and what she estimates as eighty thousand outside classes, taken the way a desperate dancer trains.
stops.quote: Él detecta todo, como no se le escapa una, tiene una templanza.
sources: NewsDigitales/Living interview transcript, 2026
suggested_refs: Gerardo Litvak and Natalia Mucio, named as formative teachers, both otherwise undocumented in this record

stops.name: La Boca, the archive crossed with popular languages
stops.date_confidence: undated statement on a current institutional page; placed with the licenciatura
stops.campa: The same page states her method in one sentence: her work consists of denaturalizing the habits of composition and creation in academic scenic dance, through the historical reconstruction of a local archive and its crossing with popular languages. It is the only statement of purpose she has published anywhere, and everything that follows can be read against it, the theatre work and the pole competitions alike. The archive is not named. The popular languages are not listed. Which local archive does a licenciada in choreographic composition reconstruct, and against what?
stops.quote: Su trabajo artístico consiste en desnaturalizar los hábitos de composición y creación en danza académica escénica a través de la reconstrucción histórica de un archivo local y el cruce con lenguajes populares.
stops.quote_source: UNA Departamento de Artes del Movimiento, graduate profile (author-supplied method statement), fetched 2026-08-16

stops.name: Jardín Botánico, three cast lists in one year, 2015
stops.date_confidence: three production fichas independently dated 2015 on alternativateatral.com
stops.campa: Three dated credits surface from 2015, the earliest year attested anywhere in her record, three years before the portfolio she builds in 2023 claims for itself. In the Jardín Botánico Carlos Thays, twenty-five dancers of the UNA company work a laboratory built from an open call, choreographed by Ana Frenkel and Emanuel Ludueña to a soundscape by Tonolec: Laboratori de Cruce. The same year the company dances Plaza Mariano Boedo, in En El séptimo cielo, and the Teatro Colón's own Centro de Experimentación, in El Laberinto de la historia, both under Roxana Grinstein's direction. She is a name in three cast lists before she is anything else on paper.

stops.name: Teatro de la Ribera, two pieces and a portrait of her, 2016
stops.date_confidence: attested across three independent alternativateatral fichas, all dated 2016
stops.campa: In 2016 the company brings two pieces to the Teatro de la Ribera in La Boca: Boicot, Nicolás Poggi's inventory of images and a monster carried within, which also plays the Centro Cultural 25 de Mayo, and Pequeños retratos, Daniel Goldín's choreography to Janáček and Satie, opening on an Ovid epigraph about self-admiration. The same year a different record appears, not made by her but about her: Mariana Di Silverio and Lucía Llopis build a videodanza installation inviting visitors to walk through facets of Emilia's world, backed by a 2015 Creation Incentive Award and shown in the XV VideoDanzaBA Festival's lab. Its title asks outright: 3 o 4 indicios sobre Emilia M.

stops.name: Centro Cultural Rector Ricardo Rojas, a teacher directs her, 2017
stops.date_confidence: attested across two independent alternativateatral fichas, both dated 2017
stops.campa: Two more UNA company works land in 2017. Un simple aleteo de pestañas puede expresar cólera, choreographed by Ayelén Clavin and Natacha Visconti, wins the Departamento de Artes del Movimiento's own Premio Graduados a la Creación that year, danced by twenty-seven at the Centro Cultural General San Martín. At the Centro Cultural Rector Ricardo Rojas, for the Festival Rojas Danza, the company dances UNANochedeBaile under a director who is, this time, not Grinstein but Gerardo Litvak, her own composition teacher, asking in the programme's own words who dances in cities, in what places, in what contexts.

stops.name: Gorriti 5839, the Taller de Formación de Bailarines, 2013-2015
stops.date_confidence: author-supplied via LinkedIn, not independently fetchable; LinkedIn blocks scraping, so this rests on her own professional listing rather than a page this pass could open and verify
stops.campa: On Gorriti in Palermo Hollywood, in a room called Viceversa Arte y Convivencia, she trains at the Taller de Formación de Bailarines from 2013 to 2015, by her own professional listing. That listing sits behind a platform no outside reader can open, so this stop rests on her word rather than an independently reachable page. She does not yet know she will return to this exact address three years later, not as a student but as a performer, inside a company's twentieth-anniversary retrospective, for a company she has not joined yet.

stops.name: Centro Cultural de la Cooperación, Mónica Fraquia's company, 2017-2018
stops.date_confidence: attested across two independent alternativateatral fichas, dated 2017 and 2018 respectively; the interview supplies the framing of Castadiva as her stated dream company
stops.campa: Mónica Fraquia directs Castadiva, the company she calls her dream in every retelling, the one she watched from the audience years before she imagined joining it. In 2017, and again in 2018 at Sala 420, she dances in Juventud, set to Philip Glass, seventy minutes built around a triumph of will, dancers running through life against repeated obstacle without frustration. She will say later that she only danced two seasons under Fraquia, but that those two seasons let her stand beside the very dancers she had once only watched from a seat.
stops.quote: Moni Fraquia, la amo. Te amo, Moni. Gran maestra... tuve la oportunidad de conocerla y de conocer a sus bailarines legendarios.

stops.name: Gorriti 5839, twenty years of Castadiva, the return, 2018
stops.date_confidence: attested across two independent alternativateatral fichas, both dated 2018
stops.campa: In 2018 the company stages Castadiva 20 años back on Gorriti, at Viceversa itself, the same address where she trained five years before: a guided tour through the building's patios, galleries and rooms, solos and duets pulled from nine works spanning 2002 to 2018. She dances in it and also works production assistance, credited twice on the same ficha. The same year, at the Centro Cultural de la Cooperación, the company dances Castadiva poética, Fraquia's piece built from Argentine poems set against Schubert and Tchaikovsky, an exploration the programme itself calls a connivance between poetry and dance.

stops.name: Teatro Mandril, Plan B, assistant director
stops.date_confidence: the ficha lists performance dates of November 2018, May 2019 and November 2019 without stating which she assisted; the piece premiered in May 2017, before her credit is dated; the venue resolves to no findable address in any gazetteer reachable from outside
stops.campa: At Teatro Mandril she works as assistant director on Plan B, a thirty-minute contemporary piece made by Agostina Fiore, Sofía Rypka and Julieta Vázquez, its own text stating plainly that Plan A failed, that the original project swerves and ends in disaster, that only one direction remains. The piece premiered in May 2017 at the Third Small Format Festival, before her credit on it is dated; the ficha then records further dates in November 2018, May 2019 and November 2019 without saying which of these carried her. It is her only assistant-directing credit in the whole reachable record.

segments.name: The Pandemic, the Reel, and the Pole

stops.name: Zona oeste, a reel of a Russian dancer, and a camera instead of a room
stops.date_confidence: her own account in the interview; the YouTube channel independently dates the Clase Contempo and Estiramientos videos to August-September 2020
stops.campa: The pandemic sends her back to the west, unemployed, to the same province she grew up in. A reel crosses her feed: a Russian dancer working a pole, exotic style, and she thinks it looks fun, unaware yet that the west has a deeper pole scene than the capital, taught by teachers she does not know yet are legends. Her contemporary training gives her coordination and line for free; her fear of height she has to solve from nothing. Before any of it becomes Almagro Exotic Club, her own channel shows what she is actually teaching that year: through August and September, Clase Contempo sessions and Estiramientos de Tardecita, filmed for a camera because no room is open.
stops.quote: Yo justo me había vuelto a vivir a oeste por la pandemia porque estaba sin trabajo... en oeste hay una gran movida de pol, de hecho hay más movida de pol en la provincia que en capital.
sources: NewsDigitales/Living interview transcript, 2026

stops.name: Paseo La Plaza, the New Face silver
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio only; no competition results page was reachable in any pass
stops.campa: On Avenida Corrientes, in the Paseo La Plaza, a competitor enters the New Face category of Exotic Generation Argentina under the name Emilia Portman. The routine is called Medusa. Natah Szuka photographs it. She takes silver, and the championship publishes no results a reader outside can reach, so the placing stands on her own document. From here the second name carries the pole work and Massacesi carries the theatre. It is the first competition in the record, and the first appearance of the second name.

stops.name: Teatro Libre, Bogotá, the fox spirit
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio; the portfolio names only Teatro Libre, Bogotá, and Teatro Libre runs two houses, so which one is unstated
stops.campa: She leaves the country for the first time in the record, to Bogotá, for Exotic Generation Latinoamérica at the Teatro Libre. Pole Maniax photographs it. Her portfolio names the theatre and the city and no more, and Teatro Libre runs two houses. In the Flow category she takes silver and the prize for best choreography with a routine called Kitsune Kitten Fantasy: a fox spirit borrowed from Japan, danced on a pole in Colombia by an Argentine licenciada in choreographic composition.

stops.name: Teatro del Globo, the Naruto routine
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio; independently corroborated in the NewsDigitales interview and the NewsDigitales press profile, both giving the same fuller story: her second pole competition, an otaku obsession with Naruto, an orange costume, blonde braids
stops.campa: At the Teatro del Globo on Marcelo T. de Alvear she competes in the Pole-up tournament, High Heels Pro category, with a routine adapted from the anime Naruto, and takes bronze. Romina Soledad photographs it. She tells the story twice more, later: an otaku streak that surfaces every so often, an orange costume and blonde braids built to personify Naruto as an exotic dancer, ridiculous and fully committed. The jury gave her the placing, she says, because they could not not give it to her, given what she staged. People still call her Naruto years later, and she cannot quite believe it happened.
stops.quote: Tengo que personificar a Naruto versión bailarina exótica.

stops.name: The Roxy Live!, Salvaje takes the Dance Expert
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio; the venue string Teatro The Roxy resolves to The Roxy Live!, Av. Coronel Niceto Vega 5542, Palermo, geocoded by OpenStreetMap; the YouTube channel independently confirms the routine's soundtrack as Young Miko
stops.campa: Her portfolio calls the venue Teatro The Roxy. The house is The Roxy Live! on Avenida Coronel Niceto Vega in Palermo, a rock club rather than a theatre. In the Dance Expert category of the Hypnotic Experience Show she dances a routine called Salvaje, to Young Miko. She takes first place, the only first place in the record; the three placings before it are two silvers and a bronze. The trophy she keeps from this one is shaped like a flying saucer, she says, because the competition's own premise was hypnotizing the audience, and she still has it.

stops.name: Exotic Generation Argentina 2023, the gaucho and the china
stops.date_confidence: confirmed by a YouTube video title, 'Exotic Generation Argentina 2023 - Em Port - Hard - tercer puesto LA TRAMPA ES LEY,' and by the fuller account in the interview; no venue is stated anywhere reachable, so the pin is the city-level anchor
stops.campa: In the Hard category of Exotic Generation Argentina, she and her friend Caru, who studies folk dance herself and plays live, dance a chacarera exótica: Caru on the bombo at the center of the piece, one of them dressed the gaucho, the other the china, a lesbian duo built around a mashup of Chaqueño Palavecino's La Trampa Es Ley and Lit Killah's remix of the same song, both of them in 23-centimeter heels. The audience starts applauding the moment the remix's beat drops, before either dancer finishes a phrase, something she calls coded into the body of anyone in that room. The jury awards third place.
stops.quote: La puse a Caru a tocar el bombo en el medio de la perfo y fue fabuloso... éramos dos, ella era la gaucha y yo era la china y teníamos como un dúo lésbico gauchesco.

stops.name: Libertad y buen gusto, comandante Guevara takes the stage
stops.date_confidence: the run's own span, 'mayo hasta diciembre,' closing 28 December, is given in her own words without a stated year; placed at 2025 as the most recent completed run consistent with the interview's own timeframe and with a further billing of the same cabaret, at the same venue, on 22 August 2026
stops.campa: Libertad y buen gusto, an art-povera cabaret run by Rodrigo Arena and C de Pimient, plays this room from May to December, closing on the twenty-eighth of December. There is no jury here, no competition, completely free and wild. Given a single prompt, defend liberty with good taste, she dances the blues of liberty dressed as Comandante Che Guevara, a kind of hero of hers, in her own words. It is the number she is still developing when this interview is recorded, one she gets to keep working rather than post once and lose to the reel cycle. An earlier pass read a costume in this room two ways, Castro's cigar or Guevara's beret; her own account settles it as Guevara.
stops.quote: Yo bailé el blu de la libertad vestida del comandante Che Guevara, que es como una especie de mi héroe.
sources: NewsDigitales/Living interview transcript, 2026

stops.name: Teatro Auditorium, Mar del Plata, the first city that is not hers

stops.name: Buenos Aires, teaching Danza Moderna and the Método Muller
stops.date_confidence: undated institutional statement, current as of the 2026 fetch; the transmission claim is one-directional, and nothing asserts she met either Muller or Limón
stops.campa: She teaches Danza Moderna and the Método Muller in schools and studios across the city and Greater Buenos Aires. The method is Jennifer Muller's, made by a dancer who was principal of the José Limón company through the 1960s and who was herself commissioned, decades later, to make a work for Buenos Aires. Limón never brought his own company south; the line reaches this city through Muller, and through the studio rooms that teach her method. What Emilia Massacesi carries into those rooms by day is the codified expressive technique she works against by night under another name.

stops.name: Almagro, a zoo with no hierarchy
stops.date_confidence: current-state statement from the interview, undated within 2026 beyond the fetch/broadcast window; the expansion is stated as planned, not completed
stops.campa: She calls her own studio a zoológico: civilians, artists, other pole dancers, people from entirely different practices, all in one room, classes run multilevel by design, a baby version, a challenge version, a professional one, no bar a student must clear to belong. Three or four instructors teach there now, two more incorporating, and she is hunting a bigger space for 2026. She once tried returning to the university as a teaching assistant; it went fine, she says, and she did not continue. Among the names she keeps from the discipline's history: Eva Bembo and Olga Coda, credited with drawing the line between flow and hard style, and Fénix, first to land the butterfly.
